role.description: 'admin' or 'member'. The first user ever created (POST /api/setup) becomes admin; only admins can create further users, who are always 'member'.

session_version.description: Bumped on logout and on password change/reset; access tokens carry it (sv) and are rejected on mismatch

email_verified_at.description: When the email was verified via a signup/reset link; NULL means no application access

boards.description: Kanban boards, shared across all authenticated users (not isolated per user)

user_id.constraint: FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
user_id.description: Creator of the board (metadata only - not used to restrict access; every authenticated user can view/edit every board)

columns.description: Kanban board columns (Backlog, In Progress, Done, etc.)

board_id.constraint: FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES boards(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

title.description: Column title (Backlog, In Progress, Done, etc.)

stage_kind.description: Commercial meaning of the stage: 'open', 'won' or 'lost'. Reports use this, never the title. At most one won and one lost per board; can't change while the column has cards. Added to older databases by backend/migrate_stage_kind.py (explicit).

cards.description: Sales leads - one card per lead; its column is the sales stage

column_id.constraint: FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES columns(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

deal_value.description: Deal value (>= 0), in `currency`, for the year `deal_year` (the "current year")

deal_value_next_year.description: Deal value (>= 0, default 0) for deal_year + 1, in the same `currency`. Not Bid revenue

deal_year.description: Calendar year deal_value belongs to; stamped at creation, changed only by migrate_deal_year_rollover.py

currency.description: Legacy. Deal Value is always USD: only USD is accepted on write, reads report USD, older codes in existing rows are ignored (backend/lead_options.py DEAL_CURRENCY)

lead_source.description: One of Website, Referral, Trade show, Cold outreach, Existing customer, Other

confidence_level.description: The sales team's own assessment: exactly LOW, MEDIUM or HIGH; NULL = not assigned (company schema version 4)

salesperson_id.constraint: FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL

board_id.constraint: FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES boards(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

user_id.constraint: FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

card_edit_history.description: Audit trail of card content edits made by member users (backs the 'M' badge / history modal). Distinct from card_actions, which is AI-only.

card_id.constraint: FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES cards(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

user_id.constraint: FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL
user_id.description: Member who made the edit; SET NULL (not cascaded) so history survives user removal

changes.description: JSON: {"title": {"old", "new"}, "details": {"old", "new"}} - only the fields that changed

card_actions.description: AI-suggested card actions (for auditing and undo)

board_id.constraint: FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES boards(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

message_id.constraint: FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES conversation_messages(id) ON DELETE SET NULL
message_id.description: AI message that triggered this action

card_id.constraint: FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES cards(id) ON DELETE SET NULL

changes.description: JSON with action details and changes

undo_entries.description: Each user's single level of undo: the inverse of their last board change. Replaced by the next change, deleted once used.

user_id.constraint: UNIQUE, FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

board_id.constraint: FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES boards(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
board_id.description: Board the change was made on

description.description: Human-readable label shown next to the Undo button

steps.description: JSON list of inverse operations (move/update/delete/create), applied in reverse order. Card steps carry expect (the card's state as the change left it); undo refuses if a card no longer matches

card_stage_events.description: Append-only card stage history (Part 18), written only by stage_history.py's flush listener in the same transaction as the change. card_id/board_id/column ids are not FKs so history survives deletions.

id.description: Unique ID; tie-break within the same instant

card_id.description: Card (no FK: kept after the card is deleted)

board_id.description: Board the card was on (no FK)

event_type.description: created | moved | won | lost | reopened | deleted | baseline (migration, or a card created by the Bid import - source import)

from_stage_kind.description: stage_kind before, copied at event time

to_stage_kind.description: stage_kind after, copied at event time

user_id.constraint: FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL

source.description: api | ai | undo | seed | migration | import | system

value_snapshot_taken.description: 1 = recorded at event time (null value = card had none); 0 = event predates snapshots, value unknown

import_batches.description: One Salcomp Bid import attempt (Part 22D): a completed import, written in the same transaction as its cards, or a failed attempt (status failed, failure_kind/failure_reason) recorded after the rollback in a separate transaction. mapping_json = rule versions, stage rules, board stages and decisions (no row content).

board_id.constraint: FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES boards(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

user_id.constraint: FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL

status.description: completed (written with its cards) | failed (an attempt that wrote nothing, recorded afterwards in its own transaction) | pending (only inside the import's transaction)

failure_reason.description: failed only: the service's message (no cell content), or just the exception type for unexpected failures

card_bid_details.description: Salcomp Bid commercial fields, 1:1 with a card (Part 22). Revenue is integer cents (exact), separate from cards.deal_value and never summed with it.

card_id.constraint: UNIQUE, FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES cards(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

revenue_current_year_cents.description: Annual revenue, current year, in cents of revenue_currency (NULL = not informed; divide by 100 only for display)

revenue_next_year_cents.description: Annual revenue, next year, in cents (same rules)

project_lead.description: Project lead (free text, not a user)

cpm.description: CPM as written in the report (free text, not a user)

card_source_refs.description: Source identity of an imported card (Part 22): at most one per card, (source_system, source_key) unique in the database.

card_id.constraint: UNIQUE, FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES cards(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

source_key.description: bid_source_key(Codigo, Cliente): "v1:" + JSON array of both parts, each with accents dropped (NFKD), whitespace collapsed and casefolded; leading zeros kept

last_import_batch_id.constraint: FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES import_batches(id) ON DELETE SET NULL

source_row_hash.description: bid_row_hash(record): "v1:" + SHA-256 of every value read from the row except its position

card_import_changes.description: What a Salcomp Bid import actually changed on an existing card (Part 22D follow-up). Separate from card_edit_history (member edits, the M badge). Only confirmed updates that changed a managed field; one row per card and batch; written in the import's transaction.

card_id.constraint: FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES cards(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

import_batch_id.constraint: FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES import_batches(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

user_id.constraint: FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL

changes.description: JSON {"card.title": {"old", "new"}, ...}: only changed fields; dates ISO; no row hash

auth_tokens.description: Persistent single-use signup/reset tokens; only the SHA-256 of the token is stored

user_id.constraint: FOREIGN KEY users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
user_id.description: User (reset); NULL for a pending signup

audit_events.description: Audit trail of opportunity assignment changes and deletions; no foreign keys so rows outlive cards and actors

user_to_boards.description: One user can create multiple boards; this is creator metadata, not an access-control relationship - boards are shared across all users

board_to_messages.description: One board has multiple conversation messages

board_to_actions.description: One board has multiple card actions

card_to_edit_history.description: One card can have multiple member-edit history entries

board_to_import_batches.description: Import batches of a board; deleted with it

user_to_import_batches.description: Who ran each import; SET NULL if the user is deleted

card_to_bid_details.description: Bid fields of a card; deleted with it

card_to_source_ref.description: Source identity of an imported card; deleted with it

import_batch_to_source_refs.description: Source refs last touched by a batch; SET NULL if the batch is deleted

card_to_import_changes.description: Import history of a card; deleted with it

import_batch_to_card_changes.description: Card changes made by a batch

constraints.cascade_delete: Deleting a user or board will cascade delete all related data
constraints.unique_constraints: username and email must be unique per user
constraints.foreign_keys: All foreign keys enabled with appropriate cascade rules
constraints.timestamps: All records have created_at and updated_at for audit trail
constraints.bid_import_identity: card_source_refs: UNIQUE (source_system, source_key) and UNIQUE card_id; card_bid_details: UNIQUE card_id; card_import_changes: UNIQUE (card_id, import_batch_id)

notes.mvp: Multi-user with two roles (admin/member). The first user created via POST /api/setup becomes admin; only admins can create further users via POST /api/users. Boards are shared, not isolated per user.
notes.future_scaling: Schema designed for PostgreSQL production deployment
notes.json_fields: metadata and changes fields store JSON for flexibility
notes.conversation_history: Supports full AI conversation history for context
notes.audit_trail: timestamps and card_actions table enable full audit trail
notes.performance: Indexes on frequently queried fields (user_id, board_id, created_at)
notes.bid_import_tables: Part 22: import tables import_batches, card_bid_details, card_source_refs, card_import_changes (schema, explicit migration, startup guard), Excel reader (22B), preview engine (22C) and the transactional import service (22D, with failed-attempt records and import history) and the admin-only HTTP endpoints (22E: preview, confirm, batch list, batch details) exist; the UI is not implemented yet. Existing databases get the tables only from backend/migrate_import_tables.py --database <path> --apply.
notes.bid_revenue_cents: card_bid_details revenue is INTEGER cents converted exactly with backend/bid_money.py (Decimal, never float; more than 2 decimals, negatives and values above 9999999999999999.99 are rejected); NULL = not informed, never 0.
notes.bid_import_mapping: Preview mapping (bid_import_preview.py): cards.title/details/company <- Nome do projeto/Descricao da prospeccao/Cliente; Bid fields -> card_bid_details; source fields -> card_source_refs. Never mapped: cards.deal_value, currency, expected_close_date, lead_source, product_line, contact, salesperson_id.
notes.edit_histories: card_edit_history = member edits only (backs the M badge, unchanged); card_import_changes = changes made by Bid imports. An import never writes card_edit_history.
